question: In a Power MOSFET, the gate-to-source voltage (Vgₛ) controls the _______.
solution:
__**Power MOSFET**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b108cad14beca31fbc7c879be83a7e33c9226935d21d1610d58d11cb6c2a1e4c.png] 

A Power MOSFET (Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor) is a semiconductor switching device designed to handle high currents and moderate-to-high voltages, widely used in power electronics.

A Power MOSFET has three main terminals: Gate, Drain, and Source

**Working Principle:**

 
• When a positive gate-to-source voltage (VGS) is applied (for N-channel), a conductive channel forms between the drain and source.
 
• Current flows due to majority carriers only, making switching fast.
 
• When VGS is removed, the channel disappears and the device turns OFF.
